questions.q: Where was Black Beauty waiting when he saw the shabby old cab?
choices: Outside one of the parks where music was playing
At the railway station waiting for the train
In Jerry's stable yard after a long day
Outside a church where Mrs. Briggs was at the service
questions.evidence: waiting outside one of the parks where music was playing

questions.q: Who was the worn-out chestnut horse?
choices: Ginger
Merrylegs
Captain
Black Beauty's mother
questions.evidence: It was Ginger! but how changed!

questions.q: What does it show when Ginger picked up a little lock of Black Beauty's hay and looked for more?
choices: She was very hungry and poorly fed
She did not like the food she was given
She was playing a game with him
She wanted to make him angry
questions.evidence: the poor creature put out her long thin neck and picked it up, and then turned and looked about for more

questions.q: What happened to Ginger after her year's rest at Earlshall?
choices: She was sold many times, always getting lower down
She went back to the Countess at Earlshall
She was sent to a quiet farm for the rest of her life
She won many races and was greatly admired
questions.evidence: she changed hands several times, but always getting lower down

questions.q: Why had Ginger stopped standing up for herself?
choices: She felt men were strongest and it was no use
She had grown to love her cruel new driver
She was far too busy working to care
Black Beauty had told her to stop fighting
questions.evidence: men are strongest, and if they are cruel and have no feeling, there is nothing that we can do

questions.q: What did Ginger say Black Beauty was to her?
choices: The only friend she ever had
A brother she had lost long ago
Her worst enemy from Earlshall
The horse that had caused her ruin
questions.evidence: You are the only friend I ever had

questions.q: What does Black Beauty wish men would do, at the end of the chapter?
choices: Be more merciful and not let horses fall into such misery
Build more cab-stands with shelter from the rain
Buy more chestnut horses for the London cabs
Let tired horses race freely in the parks
questions.evidence: if men were more merciful they would shoot us before we came to such misery
